source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 826 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 826 was established by Ordinance No. 27880, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 12, 2010. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 826 is established on property located on the south corner of J.J. Lemmon Road and Langdon Road. The size of PD 826 is approximately 101.018 acres. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 826A: overall development plan.

(2) Exhibit 826B: high school development plan.

(3) Exhibit 826C: elementary school development plan.

(4) Exhibit 826D: stadium development plan.

(5) Exhibit 826E: high school traffic management plan.

(6) Exhibit 826F: elementary school traffic management plan. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school and a private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures, overall development and use of the Property must comply with the overall development plan (Exhibit 826A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the overall development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school, development and use of the Property for a high school must comply with the high school development plan (Exhibit 826B). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the high school development plan, the text of this article controls. If there is a conflict between the high school development plan and the overall development plan, the high school development plan controls.

(c) For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school, development and use of the Property for an elementary school must comply with the elementary school development plan (Exhibit 826C). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the elementary school development plan, the text of this article controls. If there is a conflict between the elementary school development plan and the overall development plan, the elementary school development plan controls.

(d) For a private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures, development and use of the Property must comply with the stadium development plan (Exhibit 826D). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the stadium development plan, the text of this article controls. If there is a conflict between the stadium development plan and the overall development plan, the stadium development plan controls.

(e) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following uses are permitted by right:

(1) Public school other than an open-enrollment charter school.

(2) Private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures.

(c) Multifamily uses are prohibited. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) In connection with a private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures, the following accessory uses are permitted:

-- Accessory helistop.

-- Accessory medical/infectious waste incinerator.

-- Accessory outside display of merchandise.

-- Accessory outside sales.

-- Accessory pathological waste incinerator.

(c) The following accessory use is not permitted:

-- Accessory community center (private). (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the R-7.5(A) Single Family District apply.

(b) Front yard. For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school and a private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures, minimum front yard is 25 feet, as shown on the overall development plan.

(c) Side and rear yard.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, no minimum side or rear yard.

(2) For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school and private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures, minimum side and rear yard is 20 feet.

(d) Floor area.

(1) For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school, maximum floor area for a high school is 190,000 square feet.

(2) For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school, maximum floor area for an elementary school is 112,000 square feet.

(e) Height.

(1) Public school other than an open-enrollment charter school.

(A) For a high school, maximum structure height is 40 feet.

(B) For an elementary school, maximum structure height is 35 feet.

(2) Private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures. Maximum structure height is 60 feet. Stadium light poles are exempt from the 60 foot maximum height but must comply with the residential proximity slope regulations in Section 51A-4.412.

(f) Lot coverage. For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school and a private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures, maximum lot coverage is 30 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(g) Lot size.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, minimum lot size is 7,500 square feet.

(2) For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school and a private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures, no minimum lot size.

(h) Stories. For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school, maximum number of stories above grade level is two. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Public school other than an open-enrollment charter school.

(1) A minimum of 458 off-street parking and loading spaces must be provided for a high school as shown on the high school development plan.

(2) A minimum of 99 off-street parking and loading spaces must be provided for an elementary school as shown on the elementary school development plan.

(3) Future expansion of the public school other than an open-enrollment charter school must adhere to the off-street parking requirements in Division 51A-4.200.

(c) Private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures. A minimum of 390 off-street parking spaces must be provided in the location shown on the stadium development plan. The parking areas associated with the high school must be available for use during an event at the athletic facility. If there is no event at the athletic facility, access to the associated parking may be prohibited. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.112. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non- business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) For a private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures, two attached premise signs are permitted, restricted to one each for the stadium and field house, with a maximum effective area of 500 square feet each. Commercial messages are prohibited on these signs. (Ord. 27880)

SEC. 51P-826-113. FENCES.

For a private recreation center, club, or area limited to an athletic facility and related structures, fences are permitted in the required yards. Fences must be provided in the locations shown on the development plans. (Ord. 27880)

SEC, 51P-826-114. TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN.

(a) In general. Operation of a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school must comply with either the high school traffic management plan (Exhibit 826E) or the elementary school traffic management plan (Exhibit 826F), whichever is appropriate.

(b) Queuing. Queuing is only permitted inside the Property. Student drop-off and pick-up are not permitted within the city rights-of-way.

(c) Traffic study.

(1) The Property owner or operator shall prepare a traffic study evaluating the sufficiency of the traffic management plan. The initial traffic study must be submitted to the director by November 1, 2014. After the initial traffic study, the Property owner or operator shall submit updates of the traffic study to the director by March 1st of each even-numbered year.

(2) The traffic study must be in writing, performed by a licensed engineer, based on a minimum of four samples taken on different school days at different drop-off and pick-up times over a two-week period, and must contain an analysis of the following:

(A) ingress and egress points;

(B) queue lengths;

(C) number and location of personnel assisting with loading and unloading of students;

(D) drop-off and pick-up locations;

(E) drop-off and pick-up hours for each grade level;

(F) hours for each grade level; and

(G) circulation.

(3) Within 30 days after submission of a traffic study, the director shall determine if the current traffic management plan is sufficient.

(A) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan is sufficient, the director shall notify the applicant in writing.

(B) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan results in traffic hazards or traffic congestion, the director shall require the Property owner to submit an amended traffic management plan. If the Property owner fails to submit an amended traffic management plan within 30 days, the director shall notify the city plan commission.

(d) Expansion.

(1) Before issuance of a building permit to increase the number of classrooms for the elementary school or the high school, the Property owner or operator shall:

(A) submit additional data to the director showing the number of students who live within walking distance of the school, how many students actually walk to school, and how many students use public transportation; and

(B) submit an amended high school traffic management plan or elementary school traffic management plan, whichever is appropriate.

(e) Amendment process.

(1) A traffic management plan may be amended using the minor plan amendment fee and public hearing process in Section 51A-1.105(k)(3).

(2) In order to amend a traffic management plan, the Property owner or operator must provide data showing the number of students who live within walking distance of the school, how many students actually walk to school, and how many students use public transportation.

(3) The city plan commission shall authorize changes in a traffic management plan if the proposed amendments improve queuing or traffic circulation, eliminate traffic hazards, or decrease traffic congestion. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 27880)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-826.117. ZONING MAP.

PD 826 is located on Zoning Map No. P-9. (Ord. 27880)
